cards.note: External plugin is an npm package with a self-contained dsh.bundle.patch; installed through 'dsh plugin --profile web add' and mounted in a real alpha.2 profile; no repository-plugins reference remains.

dsh.client (platform web + ./client export) is the only client manifest; no legacy dshClient field or dsh.plugin.json anywhere, and the served manifest is what the client-modules scan read during the boot test.
dsh.client plus a real ./client factory artifact; the rc.8-era 'no ./package.json export' drop no longer applies at alpha.2, where the row is admitted and now materializes.

inject declares tools/webServer; settings is claimed through ctx.inject(['settings']) and connection through a weak ctx.get, so no undeclared property read remains. Cold boot on the target profile passed.
Optional host services are probed weakly (ctx.get('connection')) or registered through ctx.inject(['settings']) and degrade; hard inject is reserved for the web-only tools/webServer.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event and derives no session state.
The card reads interpreters config over the plugin's own route and never consumes ctx.sessions.
No jobs/tasks output tailing API is used.
Injects and calls webServer (the renamed service) only; no httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone identifier remains, verified against the target tag.
No image attachments, read_image output, or persisted image metadata.
No read_image registration, wrapping, or snapshot matching.
No custom LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment/upload cache.
No APIProxy call site: the card's only wire use is ctx.remote.$on for one forwarded event, and the host half works in-process.
The plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents; the target alpha.2 also restores the marker (A2-01).
No host source patch and no internal session-view imports.
No launcher wrapper or SDK integration; installation/verification went through the official launcher and the runtime DSH_HOME.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parsing.
No tool presentation mode or PTC identifiers.
No permission, approval, or WebFetch policy; the bundle patch only inserts this plugin row.

The custom loopback route applies the Connection Host/Origin + session-cookie fence itself; measured 401 without a Cookie, 403 for a foreign Host, 200 with the launch-URL Cookie, and the card's read/write path still passes.
Not a model-provider plugin; it registers no login configuration.
The card's zh/en dictionaries already use the public ctx.locale.register; there is no custom i18n patch to retire.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface.
Deployment/privacy behavior of the official DeepSeek adapter; plugin code is unaffected.
No PowerShell/Bash persistence or directory-picker workaround is carried.
The plugin does not enable session-log-deepseek; the shipped profile owns that row.

Acceptance opens the launch URL dsh web printed (token -> Cookie) and reads the real page; the boot manifest, the plugin entry, the alpha.2 onboarding dialogs, and the inventory vocabulary were re-verified on the target tag.
No userQuestions.registerProvider answerer is registered.
No agent-preset inference from persisted sessions or preset roots.
No isTokenDelta import and no TPS computation.
The plugin is not a profile/bundle maintainer reusing dsh-base; its patch inserts only its own row.
No @earendil-works/pi-ai dependency.

dsh-client-runtime is gone from peers and dsh.client.inject; the snapshot store comes from the platform-seeded @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store and slots/remote from their owning packages, confirmed by the boot.

The factory registers as '@bench/dsh-bench-interpreters-card': package name, cordis.patch.yml row name and boot-manifest entry id agree; window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries carried the id and no 'loaded without registering' appeared.
No session timeline or user-message content is read.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, recall, selection).
No MarkdownText / fenced CodeBlock rendering.
ctx.connection.api is not consumed; the card transports over its own route.
No subagent seed/descriptor construction.
No ctx.workspaces / ctx.uiWorkspace navigation or directory calls.
No third-party persisted SessionEvents are produced or consumed.
Only forwarded-event subscriptions (ctx.remote.$on) are used; no unary Remote call resolves to RemoteResult, so RemoteError handling is not hit.

The runtime import @deepseek-ai/schemastery moved from an optional peer to dependencies after a real profile boot failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; remaining peers are type/host-owned and optional, and installation ran through pnpm, the profile's package manager.
No Node-range workaround exists; verification ran on Node 24.21, outside the 24.0-24.11.1 defect window.
The plugin does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate PluginInventorySnapshot.
No host.describe or $host usage; reconnects still ride connection/reset.
The plugin composes into the shipped web bundle and mounts none of the session-projection-consuming tool packages itself.

The namespace is the literal constant NS = 'interpreters' (valid grammar) passed directly to settings.register; verified end to end - the namespace was served, the card key paired, and a write persisted and read back.
